A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Engram study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C are readable and can be matched across pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original pretraining and long-context evaluations (Tables 1-2), architectural ablations, mechanistic analyses, and inference-throughput measurements (Table 4).

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the main experimental comparisons and Appendix B's benchmark trajectories.

M1.justification: Engram's tokenizer compression, hashed N-gram retrieval, context-aware gating, convolution, multi-branch integration, and memory-prefetching procedures are unchanged. The wording revisions in Section 2 introduce no new component or procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same pretraining benchmarks, LongPPL/RULER evaluations, Few-NERD analysis, and English/Chinese case studies. Speech recognition and recommender systems are newly discussed as related work, not evaluated domains.

E2.justification: The Dense/MoE baselines and OverEncoding remain in the same corresponding comparisons. Newly cited methods such as N-Grammer, STEM, L3, and CoG are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Sections 3-6 and Appendix A retain the same model configurations, compute and token budgets, metrics, prompting settings, long-context training, and throughput workload. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The LogitLens/CKA analyses, insertion-layer sweep, component ablations, inference-time embedding suppression, gating examples, and tokenizer-compression case study are retained unchanged. Reflowing these passages and figures adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including the minibatch unbiased HSIC estimator used for CKA. No run/seed disclosures, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: The experimental tables, plotted results, and appendix findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains BBH scores of 50.9/55.9 for MoE-27B/Engram-27B, and Table 2 retains their 50k-checkpoint Multi-Query NIAH scores of 84.2/97.0.

T1.justification: Equations 1-9 retain the same architecture mathematics, sparsity-allocation definition, CKA formulation, and soft layer-alignment index. No formal assumptions, derivations, proofs, or mathematical corrections are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the conditional-memory contribution, U-shaped allocation law, iso-budget performance claims, effective-depth explanation, and low-overhead inference claim. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: The effective-depth interpretation, placement trade-offs, Engram-40B under-training explanation, and inference-ablation caveats are retained. Section 2.3's revised placement sentence restates the modeling-versus-latency trade-off already explained in v1 Sections 2.5 and 6.2.

D1.justification: Appendix A's architecture and hyperparameters, the implementation and hardware disclosures, and the code-access information remain substantively unchanged. Revised citations and URL punctuation disclose no new technical settings or access conditions.

R1.justification: Section 7 substantially broadens the research positioning through a new High-Cardinality Categorical Embeddings discussion, connecting Engram to recommender-system embeddings and explaining its distinct textual keys and gated integration. It also adds N-Grammer, speech-recognition lookup memory, STEM, L3, and CoG. Corresponding references are added, and the Kimi and Muon citations are revised.

P1.justification: v2 expands the author list, adds an equal-contribution note, makes localized wording edits in Section 2, and integrates additional related-work prose. The overall section sequence and technical exposition remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 moves from page 6 to page 7, and figures, tables, and surrounding paragraphs reflow. The expanded author block and bibliography also affect layout. The numbered figures and tables retain their designs and contents.

improvement.justification: The expanded Section 7 provides more complete attribution and clearer positioning relative to earlier N-gram methods and recommender-system embeddings. More directly relevant Kimi and Muon references also improve citation precision. These are useful scholarly improvements, while the method, experimental evidence, and appendices remain substantively unchanged.
